newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI eases forex norms for travel, employment.
newsitem.headline: India RBI eases forex norms for travel, employment.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Thursday said it was relaxing rules for release of foreign exchange for employment and travel.
The RBI also enhanced the powers of authorised foreign exchange dealers (ADs) for release of foreign exchange and simplified procedure for some trade related activities.
Accordingly, ADs can now release foreign exchange:
* Upto $3,000 per person towards basic travel quota.
* Upto $2,500 per person in addition to BTQ (basic travel quota) entitlement of $3,000 for going abroad on employment.
* Upto $1,000 per person per year towards gifts to relatives and friends.
* $1,000 towards donations to charitable, educational, religious, cultural organisations abroad.

Earlier, authorised dealers could release foreign exchange upto $2,000 per beneficiary towards basic travel quota, $500 per calendar year per beneficiary towards basic travel quota, $500 per calendar year per beneficiary towards gifts, $500 towards donations and $500 per person or $1,000 per family for emigration, RBI said in a statement.

The RBI also enhanced the limit to ADs to effect advance remittances towards import without a bank guarantee from $5,000 to $15,000 or equivalent as the earlier limit was fixed a few years ago, the statement said.

ADs can now release foreign exchange towards service related remittances such as tie-up arrangements between Indian agents and overseas principals for booking of hotel accommodation and use of prepaid telecard abroad and the like, RBI said.
The details of the delegated powers are available on RBI's website at http://www.reservebank.com.
